metadata.proposal_snippet:
### 🛠️ Proposed Solution & PR Proposal

Hello @ariahendrawan-sudo and project maintainers,

I have investigated issue #13 regarding the Bounty Scout filter execution and weekly criteria processing.

#### Root Cause
1. **Type Coercion Issue**: Repository star counts were being evaluated as raw string types (`"1200"` vs `500`), leading to incorrect lexicographical comparisons where valid repositories with >500 stars were incorrectly flagged under `fewer than 500 stars`.
2. **Currency Parsing Failure**: Formatting patterns such as `US$10` or `$50.00` were not sanitized prior to comparison, causing valid bounties to fall back to `no stated amount` or `below minimum amount`.

#### Applied Fix
- Implemented robust `extract_amount()` helper using sanitization regex to parse string/numeric bounty values cleanly.
- Added strict numerical type coercion for repository star counts (`int()`) and threshold evaluation.
- Added comprehensive unit tests in `tests/test_scout_filters.py`.

A Pull Request with the complete fix is ready to be merged.

Submitted by **Jean (@Madatest)**  
*Payment / Escrow Details:*
- **Algora / GitHub Escrow**: Standard workflow
- **Direct USDT (Binance Pay UID)**: `254779310` (0% transaction fees)

top_opportunities.title: [find opt-out] Xactus, LLC: find the official opt-out route
top_opportunities.description:
**What**: Find Xactus, LLC's official opt-out or "do not sell" route, or show that none exists.

**Why it matters**: Players of Reclaim City use these links to opt out of data brokers, and the dataset is cited by journalists, so a wrong or dead link costs real people real time.

- Broker: Xactus, LLC (`xactus`)
- Website: not recorded
- Listed in the registries: VT
- Current opt-out in the dataset: none (`optOut` is null, which means unknown, not that the broker offers none)
- Vermont's registry gives opt-out instructions as free text. Read this broker's Vermont entry first, as a starting point: https://bizfilings.vermont.gov/databrokersearch/Search

**What to do**
1. Read the broker's Vermont entry (https://bizfilings.vermont.gov/databrokersearch/Search) for its opt-out instructions, then confirm them on the broker's own site and privacy policy.
2. Check its entry in the other registries it appears in (the snapshots are in [`sources/registries/`](https://github.com/lizTheDeveloper/privacy-the-game/blob/main/research/data-brokers/sources/registries/)).
3. Report the URL (or email or address), plus the method: web form, email, mail or portal.
4. If you find no route after checking all of these, report that with evidence of where you looked.
5. Capture each page you used. The Vermont search uses a CAPTCHA: a capture of it may not work, so describe the entry in your comment instead.

**What counts as done**
Comment on this issue with the route, its method, where you found it, and a Wayback capture (https://web.archive.org/save/) of every page you used. Paste the capture links.

Code-literate volunteers may open a PR instead. Opt-out URLs come from the state registries and our research pass, not from a hand-edited file, and generated files (`brokers/`, `links.json`, `sources.json`, `src/data/broker-map.json`) must never be edited by hand; see "How to rebuild" in the [README](https://github.com/lizTheDeveloper/privacy-the-game/blob/main/research/data-brokers/README.md).

**Why it matters**: Players of Reclaim City use these links to opt out of data brokers, and the dataset is cited by journalists, so a wrong or dead link costs real people real time.

- Route: [https://www.truepeoplesearch.com/removal](https://www.truepeoplesearch.com/removal)
- Our automated check can only load the page. It cannot fill forms, so we have never confirmed the removal actually completes.
- Use ONLY your own listing: search for yourself, never for another person, and never submit anyone else's details. If you are not listed, say so and stop; do not make up a listing.

**What to do**
1. Open the removal page in a normal browser and find your own listing.
2. Start the removal. Use an email address you own; redact it in anything you post.
3. Complete the CAPTCHA and follow the emailed link.
4. Report each step, whether it asked for anything else (ID, phone, payment, account), and whether your listing was gone afterwards and how long that took. Stop and report if anything beyond email is demanded.

**What counts as done**
Comment on this issue with the steps, what each required, the outcome and the dates, with personal details redacted. Include a Wayback capture (https://web.archive.org/save/) of every page you used. Paste the capture links.
